name: Proxmox_VE_GuestStatus
description: Power state, configuration lock and HA state for every QEMU virtual machine and LXC container in a Proxmox VE cluster.
technicalNotes:
BatchScript, discovering the same guest instances as Proxmox VE Guest Performance. Split from it so state changes can carry a different alert posture from utilisation.

Status deliberately ships with NO alert threshold. A stopped guest is usually stopped on purpose, and alerting on every powered-off VM produces noise that gets the whole suite disabled. Set a threshold of "< 1" on the instances or instance groups that are genuinely expected to stay running -- or alert on HAError, which only fires for guests the cluster itself considers broken.

HAError covers the error and fence states. Templates are excluded from discovery.

Instance ERIs. Discovery is its own (Proxmox VE Guest Performance keeps the shared one) and produces the same instances and wildvalues. Each guest on an online node also gets predef.externalResourceID -- the MAC of its first virtual NIC, or for a guest with no NIC the same proxmoxve--<cluster>--<type>-<vmid> key Proxmox_VE_Topology emits -- and predef.externalResourceType=VirtualMachine, so the topology map can draw every guest under its node even when the guest is not a resource of its own. Only this module carries the keys; Guest Performance never does. Cost: 2 extra calls plus 1 config read per guest on an online node, once per discovery run (hourly) -- the same O(guests) the TopologySource already pays. The reads stop for a node after its first failure, so a sick node costs one timeout per run rather than one per guest; its remaining guests are discovered without keys until the next run. A guest on an offline node, or one whose config cannot be read, is still discovered, without keys.

Not supported with topo.namespace or topo.blacklist set: those rewrite the TopologySource's keys, which these would then silently fail to match, so discovery adds no keys there.

Limitation: not yet tested with the API token on several nodes of one cluster, which puts the same key on several instances -- a configuration docs/INSTALL.md 4.1 advises against.

Migrating is 1 while the guest is being migrated, from the lock Proxmox holds for the whole migration; it costs no extra call.

datapoints.name: Status
datapoints.description: 1 when the guest is running, 0 otherwise. Intentionally unthresholded; see technical notes.

datapoints.name: Locked
datapoints.description: 1 when the guest configuration is locked by a running task such as a backup or migration.

datapoints.name: Migrating
datapoints.description: 1 while the guest is being migrated (Proxmox's migrate lock).

datapoints.name: HAManaged
datapoints.description: 1 when the guest is managed by the HA stack.

datapoints.name: HAError
datapoints.description: 1 when the HA stack reports this guest in an error or fence state.
datapoints.alertBody:
Proxmox guest ##INSTANCE## is in an HA error or fence state. The cluster could not keep the guest running on its assigned node.

This started at ##START##, ##DURATION## ago.
